## Summary

Implements issue #150: session-bound push registrations.

- **Migration `0031_push_subscriptions.sql`**: `push_subscriptions` table (user, nullable session, `channel` web_push/apns, platform, web fields, APNs fields, timestamps, `revoked_at`), with CHECK constraints enforcing channel/field and channel/platform validity, plus partial unique indexes on `endpoint`/`device_token` scoped to active (non-revoked) rows.
- **`push/` data package**: upsert-based registration (reuses the partial unique index via `ON CONFLICT` so an active duplicate updates in place and a revoked registration can reactivate as a fresh row without breaking uniqueness), scoped explicit revocation, session-cascade revocation, and one repository operation (`revokePushSubscriptionByProviderInvalidation`) for #151's future provider-invalidation handling.
- **`authActions.ts`**: `logout` and `revokeUserSession` now cascade into the push-registration revocation in the same transaction, so a registration never outlives its session while other sessions keep working.
- **HTTP surface**: `POST /api/push-subscriptions` (register/reactivate) and `POST /api/push-subscriptions/:id/revoke`, authenticated the same way as every other protected route, wired into `app.ts` and documented in `routeMatrix.ts`.

The branch was rebased on top of #149's merged notifications work (this branch's original base predated that merge), then the feature was added on top.

Verified this run: unit tests 127/127, integration tests 848/848 (real ephemeral Postgres, all 31 migrations applied cleanly), e2e tests 5/5, ESLint clean repo-wide, `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages/services, Prettier clean repo-wide.
